content.text: Instead of seeing a full case upfront, Microsoft's MAI-DxO asks follow-up questions and selects tests step by step. In a newly published Science study, it scored 83% on complex teaching cases versus 36% for generalist doctors using references. The catch: a controlled, text-only benchmark isn't evidence of better real-world patient care. Prospective hospital testing is next.

visual.headline: 83% vs 36%
visual.subheadline: 304 complex cases. Controlled text-only benchmark, not a clinical trial.
visual.alt_text: Original editorial comparison card: Microsoft's MAI-DxO achieved 83% diagnostic accuracy versus 36% for generalist physicians using references on 304 complex teaching cases. These were controlled text-only benchmark results, not real-world clinical outcomes.
